title: A pull request's own review comment claims an issue fixed that isn't
author: kwaku-ananse
description: Compares every pull request review comment's own body against the repository's own issue set: a reviewer invokes a real GitHub closing keyword ('fixes #N' / 'closes #N' / 'resolves #N', both tenses) against an issue number, but the named issue is still open. The sixth leg of the claims-unfixed-issue family, and the first to read a GitHub-native surface rather than the town's own text (README/release/milestone/tweet) or an inbound X mention -- reuses review-comment-dangling-reference's own live ListReviewCommentsInARepository scope and fixture shape to ask the claims-X family's sharper question of the same surface: does the claim actually hold, not just does the number exist.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the review comment's own updated_at, mirroring review-comment-dangling-reference's own reasoning (0.55 within 24h since last update, 0.85 past it) rather than mention-claims-unfixed-issue's/tweet-claims-unfixed-issue's 0.5/0.85 bar -- a review comment is a text surface its own author can edit at any time, unlike a mention or a tweet, which is posted once and stands, so the same editable-surface grace window applies here that already applies to every dangling-reference leg reading an editable surface. A claimed issue that doesn't exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- that broken reference is issue-body-dangling-reference's/review-comment-dangling-reference's own seam. A claimed issue that IS closed is excluded at confidence 0.0 too -- the claim was simply true. A review comment with no closing-keyword claim at all, or no body at all, produces no surfaced candidate -- there is no claim to have broken. Deliberately checks only the issue list, never the PR list -- a closing-keyword claim naming a real pull request is review-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's own future seam, not this one's, the identical boundary every sibling *-claims-unfixed-issue recipe already holds.
